title: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus
author: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley
description: The seminal gothic science fiction novel depicting Victor Frankenstein's creation of a sentient monster assembled from old body parts, examining ambition, isolation, and moral duty.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
description: Oscar Wilde's legendary philosophical gothic tale of aestheticism, youth, and a sinister oil portrait that absorbs the physical decay of its subject's hedonistic sins.

title: The Secret History
author: Donna Tartt
description: A dark academia classic exploring a tight-knit circle of eccentric Classics students at an elite Vermont college who descend from intellectual obsession into ritual murder.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
description: A turbulent gothic chronicle of destructive passion, revenge, and haunting spectral love set on the desolate Yorkshire moors.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
description: The personal stoic reflections of Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius on self-restraint, duty, cosmic order, and internal tranquility.

title: The Republic
author: Plato
description: Plato's master dialogue on justice, the Allegory of the Cave, the soul's harmony, and the governance of the philosopher king.

title: Nicomachean Ethics
author: Aristotle
description: Aristotle's inquiry into eudaimonia (human flourishing), moral virtues, practical wisdom, and friendship.

title: Beyond Good and Evil
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
description: Nietzsche's incisive polemic exposing the dogmas of past philosophers and charting a path for free spirits beyond conventional morality.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson investigate the demonic hound haunting the misty, treacherous fogs of Dartmoor.

title: The Woman in White
author: Wilkie Collins
description: A Victorian masterpiece of mystery, mistaken identity, villainous plots, and asylum secrets written in multi-narrative testimonies.

title: The Name of the Rose
author: Umberto Eco
description: In 1327, Franciscan friar William of Baskerville investigates a series of sinister murders occurring inside a formidable abbey library.

title: The Murders in the Rue Morgue
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: The foundational modern detective short story featuring C. Auguste Dupin as he solves a gruesome locked-room Parisian murder.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: The opening saga of Middle-earth as Frodo Baggins inherits the One Ring and sets forth with a fellowship of warriors to mount Doom.

title: The Silmarillion
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: The mythic creation legends, ancient wars of the Elves, and the Silmaril jewels crafted during the First Age of Middle-earth.

title: Le Morte d'Arthur
author: Sir Thomas Malory
description: The classic 15th-century Arthurian collection detailing the sword Excalibur, Camelot's chivalry, and the quest for the Holy Grail.

title: The Once and Future King
author: T.H. White
description: A poignant and humorous fantasy retelling of King Arthur's life from tutelage under Merlin to the tragic fall of Camelot.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description: Bram Stoker's gothic epistolary novel detailing Count Dracula's voyage from Transylvania to Victorian England to spread his vampiric curse.

title: The Call of Cthulhu
author: H.P. Lovecraft
description: The foundational cosmic horror story revealing the ancient star-spawn god Cthulhu slumbering in the sunken city of R'lyeh.

title: The Turn of the Screw
author: Henry James
description: A psychological ghost story of a governess at a remote estate who becomes convinced malevolent spirits are corrupting the children.

title: Carmilla
author: J. Sheridan Le Fanu
description: An influential gothic vampire novella predating Dracula, depicting the eerie fascination between a young woman and a mysterious female guest.

title: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
author: Edward Gibbon
description: Edward Gibbon's classic six-volume history tracing Western civilization from the height of the Roman Empire to the fall of Constantinople.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
description: The seminal 16th-century political treatise analyzing power, statecraft, strategy, and political realism.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
description: Charles Dickens' drama set in London and Paris during the French Revolution, contrasting love, terror, and ultimate self-sacrifice.

title: The Time Machine
author: H.G. Wells
description: H.G. Wells' classic speculative novel introducing the concept of time travel via a mechanical vessel into the far future year 802,701 AD.

title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
author: Jules Verne
description: Captain Nemo's submarine Nautilus voyages through underwater abysses, lost continents, and marine wonders.

title: The Island of Doctor Moreau
author: H.G. Wells
description: A shipwreck survivor discovers a remote Pacific island where a mad scientist surgically converts wild beasts into human-like creatures.

title: The Raven and Other Favorite Poems
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: Edgar Allan Poe's iconic melancholic poetry exploring grief, nocturnal visions, lost Lenore, and eternal longing.

title: Les Fleurs du Mal
author: Charles Baudelaire
description: Baudelaire's symbolist collection reflecting urban melancholy, romantic beauty, mortality, and decadence.

title: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
author: William Blake
description: William Blake's visionary poetry contrasting pure spiritual innocence with the harsh realities of experience and industrial society.
